meta.scope: South Korea Batch 2 — Trade statistics & major FTAs, corporate/financial-statement analysis (chaebol-relevant), vital statistics & ultra-low fertility, population projections, and supporting external/industrial depth. Continues top-down under locked definition.
meta.strategy_note: Builds on Batch 1 core. Captures Korea’s export-oriented structure, key bilateral/plurilateral trade instruments, corporate sector (relevant to chaebol analysis), and the extreme demographic uniqueness (world’s lowest fertility).

candidates.title: Trade Statistics (수출입무역통계) — Korea Customs Service / MOTIR
candidates.publisher: Korea Customs Service / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources (MOTIR)
candidates.description: Monthly and annual customs-based merchandise trade statistics by commodity, partner country, and enterprise characteristics. Primary source for Korea’s export and import performance, including the high concentration in semiconductors and other key items.
candidates.notes: Core external-trade series for an economy whose growth is heavily export-driven. Continuously cited in BOP analysis, industrial policy and FTA impact assessments. Complements BOK Balance of Payments with detailed commodity and partner matrices.

candidates.title: Korea–United States Free Trade Agreement (KORUS FTA)
candidates.publisher: Governments of the Republic of Korea and the United States
candidates.description: Bilateral free-trade agreement that entered into force in March 2012. Eliminates or reduces tariffs on the large majority of goods trade and includes provisions on services, investment, intellectual property, labour and environment. One of Korea’s most commercially significant bilateral agreements with its major security and economic partner.
referenced_by: MOTIR and Customs trade statistics and FTA utilisation reports
BOK and KOSTAT external-sector and industrial analysis
Official impact assessments and subsequent trade-policy documents
Academic and think-tank studies treating KORUS as a baseline bilateral instrument
candidates.notes: Static bilateral instrument that meets the expanded node definition through recurring citation in trade statistics, policy documents and impact analyses. Parallel to Japan’s USJTA / CPTPP / Japan–EU EPA nodes. Central to understanding Korea’s trade architecture with the United States.

candidates.title: Korea–EU Free Trade Agreement
candidates.publisher: Governments of the Republic of Korea and the European Union
candidates.description: Bilateral free-trade agreement that entered into force provisionally in 2011 and fully thereafter. Comprehensive coverage of goods, services, investment and regulatory cooperation. One of the earliest and most ambitious FTAs between the EU and an Asian economy.
referenced_by: MOTIR trade statistics and FTA utilisation data
EU and Korean official impact assessments
Subsequent FTA negotiations and comparative studies
candidates.notes: Complements KORUS as a major bilateral pillar. Recurringly cited in analyses of Korea’s multi-track trade strategy and in comparisons with Japan’s EPA network.

candidates.title: Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) — Korea participation
candidates.publisher: RCEP Participating Countries (including Republic of Korea)
candidates.description: Plurilateral trade agreement among 15 Asia-Pacific economies that entered into force for Korea in 2022. Covers tariff reduction, rules of origin, services, investment and economic cooperation. Largest trade agreement by membership population.
referenced_by: MOTIR and Customs trade statistics on RCEP partner shares
Official Korean and ASEAN+ impact assessments
Comparative analyses with CPTPP and bilateral FTAs
candidates.notes: Plurilateral instrument that qualifies via recurring citation. Completes the core set of major trade agreements structuring Korea’s contemporary trade policy (KORUS, Korea–EU, RCEP).

candidates.title: Financial Statement Analysis (기업경영분석) — Bank of Korea
candidates.description: Annual (with related quarterly elements) analysis of the financial statements of Korean corporations, covering sales, profitability, stability, growth and financial ratios by industry and firm size. Long-running series (published since 1960) that provides the empirical basis for assessing corporate-sector health, including large business groups.
candidates.notes: Key corporate-sector statistics. Directly relevant to analysis of Korea’s concentrated industrial structure (large enterprises / business groups). Complements the Mining & Manufacturing Survey and national accounts with accounting-based measures of profitability, leverage and investment. Parallel to Japan’s Financial Statements Statistics of Corporations.

candidates.title: Vital Statistics — Births, Deaths, Marriages, Divorces (인구동향조사 / 출생·사망통계)
candidates.description: Annual (with monthly/quarterly provisional) statistics on live births, deaths, marriages and divorces, including the total fertility rate (TFR), crude rates and age-specific rates. Documents Korea’s ultra-low fertility (TFR recently around 0.7–0.8) and rapid demographic transition.
candidates.notes: Core demographic series that quantifies one of Korea’s most distinctive features — the world’s lowest total fertility rate. Continuously cited in population projections, social-policy, labour-supply and fiscal-sustainability analysis. Parallel to Japan’s Vital Statistics node but with even more extreme fertility levels.

candidates.title: Population Projections (장래인구추계)
candidates.description: Official long-term population projections (typically to 2070 or beyond) under alternative fertility, mortality and migration scenarios. Shows the projected peak and subsequent decline of total population and the rapid rise in the old-age dependency ratio.
candidates.notes: Forward-looking demographic framework. Essential for planning education, pensions, healthcare, labour supply and regional policy under rapid population decline and super-ageing. Continuously referenced in medium- and long-term fiscal and social-policy documents.

candidates.title: Trade by Enterprise Characteristics
candidates.description: Statistics linking merchandise trade flows to enterprise size and characteristics (large enterprises, middle-standing enterprises, SMEs). Highlights the high concentration of exports among large firms.
candidates.notes: Useful bridge between aggregate trade statistics and corporate-structure analysis. Documents the dominant role of large enterprises in Korea’s export performance and is relevant to chaebol-related economic discussion.

candidates.title: Index of Industrial Production and related short-term industrial indicators (detailed)
candidates.description: Detailed monthly indices of industrial production, shipments and inventories, with breakdowns by industry (including semiconductors and other key sectors). Extends the core Mining & Manufacturing Survey node.
candidates.notes: Deepens the short-term activity coverage. Semiconductor and related electronics components are critical to Korea’s industrial cycle and export performance; these detailed series are closely watched by markets and policymakers.

candidates.title: Seoul Capital Area / Regional accounts and statistical contrast (preliminary)
candidates.publisher: Statistics Korea / local governments (Seoul Metropolitan Government and surrounding provinces)
candidates.description: Statistical products that allow comparison of the Seoul Capital Area (Seoul + Gyeonggi + Incheon) with the rest of the country in population, economic activity, income and social indicators. Captures the extreme concentration of population and economic activity in the capital region.
candidates.notes: Regional-contrast node. Korea exhibits very high spatial concentration in the Seoul Capital Area; systematic comparison with non-capital regions is essential for hierarchy-homogeneity checks and for understanding regional inequality and policy responses. Parallel to Japan’s Tokyo + Okinawa contrast approach.
